important_distinctions: The solver statistics Lower Bound column is a static heuristic field. It remains below solution cost on many solved boards, so it cannot be interpreted as the final search frontier or the strongest proved bound.
A timeout in a push-optimal test indicates failure under that configuration and time limit. It does not itself prove optimality unresolved worldwide.

IJCAI 2016 Table 1 highlights UB cells where search established an optimum. None of the 17 candidate UB cells is highlighted (checked visually). The paper mentions higher frontier f-values on timeout but does not tabulate the individual final f-values for unresolved boards.
The SoCS article landing page currently gives a 2021 upload/publication date, but the paper is from SoCS 2013. It is not a newer numerical-bound source.
Recent learned-solver results on Boxoban or arbitrary small boards do not establish bounds for these exact XSokoban layouts.
Closed-source solver reports are research leads; benchmark lower bounds still require independently checked proof evidence.

The current Sokolution homepage observed by the parent agent lists v7.32; the JSoko developer news page reports v7.33 on 2025-03-20, a crash fix for boards exceeding 1024 floors. Version-number discrepancy is preserved rather than resolved by assumption.

sources_inspected.findings: Table 1 gives initial bounds used here. All 17 candidate optimum cells unhighlighted. Final frontier values mentioned but unlisted.
Table 2, PDF page 5: MM/RS/PDB bounds for all 17 checked. None exceeds the 2016 maximum. Full primary PDF read through web tool; local direct download failed.
73 of 90 solved in published push-optimal test; all 17 candidate boards not solved. Sokolution 7.32, 30 minutes, AMD Ryzen 9 7900X.
JSoko 2.22, 10 minutes, 25 of 90 push-optimal solves. None of the 17 candidate boards solved.

Current comparison reports push-optimal solved totals: Rolling Stone 6, Pereira 28, JSoko 25, Sokolution 73. Sokolution source unavailable. Links to same optimal-statistics tables; no final-frontier records.
Lists the 28 solved boards from IJCAI 2016; no candidate present.
Author technical description of matching/penalty pattern databases, optimal and nonoptimal modes. Historic description is older than 7.x; no current per-board lower record.
